title: When the Terminal Turns Revisited
premise: Sebastian Dravenmoor, a xenolinguist who once decoded the Meridian signal and now hides among cargo haulers, discovers the colony's children are dreaming in that same alien tongue—a language he no longer dreams in himself. As Earth's final transmission loop counts down, the colonial council demands he translate the children's shared dream, which contains a choice: wake the cryosleepers carrying Earth's old loyalties or those carrying its lost knowledge. Sebastian realizes the dream is not a message but a test written by the Meridians long ago, and that his own divided identity—half translator, half colonist—makes him the only honest interpreter. In the end he refuses to choose for humanity, teaches the children to read the dream themselves, and the loop ends with both halves waking to a generation that finally belongs to neither Earth nor the stars, but to each other.
about_author: Ulyana Fairweather is a former radio astronomer turned novelist who writes about people caught between signals and silences. She lives aboard a decommissioned research vessel with her partner and an unreasonable number of star charts.

chapters.title: Cargo of Quiet Things
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He runs a routine haul through contested orbits, deliberately unremarkable, haunted by the fact that his dreams have gone wordless—no human language left in them. A near-miss with a patrol drone reminds him how fragile his invisibility is. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: Colony teacher Mara Okonkwo's POV. Six children arrive at school reciting identical syllables from a shared dream they can't explain. Mara recognizes the cadence from archived transmissions she was never cleared to hear. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into institutional fear.

chapters.title: A Language He Buried
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Mara plays him a recording of the children; he identifies it as Meridian before he can stop himself. The council summons him, and five years of hiding collapse in a single hearing. Emotional beat: the terror of being recognized by what you know.

chapters.title: The Council of Half-Truths
chapters.summary: Councilor Vess's POV. The council debates whether Sebastian is an asset or a contamination risk, while quietly planning to weaponize whatever the dream contains. Vess justifies surveillance as protection. Emotional beat: loyalty to institutions vs. loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: What the Dream Says
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, working with the eldest child, Iyo. Together they parse the dream's structure and find it isn't a warning—it's a question posed to whoever wakes first. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership becoming genuine trust.

chapters.title: The Loop Counts Down
chapters.summary: Engineer Dov's POV. Earth's last transmission loop enters terminal decay; every faction scrambles to claim the cryo-bays' two wake orders. Dov discovers someone has been tampering with the bay manifests. Emotional beat: dread as systems meant to preserve begin deciding.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Long Dark
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The children are quarantined 'for their safety'; Mara breaks into the archive to learn why the Meridian signal was classified, uncovering that Earth knew the dream-test existed before launch. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing everything she taught.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The council forces a deadline: name the wake order or lose access to the children. Sebastian realizes choosing would make him exactly the kind of translator the Meridians warned against—one who speaks for others. Emotional beat: the cost of refusing power.

chapters.title: The Test Is the Answer
chapters.summary: Climax. Multiple POVs converge as Vess attempts a forced decryption, the loop hits its final cycle, and Sebastian instead opens the translation to the children publicly—letting the dream ask its question of everyone at once. The bays unlock on a consensus protocol no one designed but everyone completes. Emotional beat: truth surviving coercion.

chapters.title: Waking in Both Tongues
chapters.summary: Resolution, Iyo's POV. Both halves of cryosleep wake over months; the first sleepers meet children who greet them in Meridian-inflected speech. Sebastian finally dreams again—in a language that is neither fully human nor fully other. Emotional beat: belonging found not in origins, but in shared authorship of what comes next.
